summary:
**Lunar Window – Lunar Landing Site Navigator**

Lunar Window is an interactive tool designed to help users explore and compare potential landing locations near the Moon’s South Pole. The idea came from a simple but important question: how can we identify locations that offer better visibility of both the Sun and Earth?

Using astronomical data from NASA/JPL Horizons (DE441), our tool tracks the positions of the Sun and Earth from three selected lunar coordinates and shows how their visibility changes over time. Users can explore different time periods, view interactive visualizations, compare locations, and see which ones perform better based on their selected mission priorities.

This project aims to make complex astronomical data easier to understand and use. By bringing Sun and Earth visibility analysis into one place, Lunar Window can support early mission planning and help researchers explore conditions that may be important for future lunar exploration, particularly solar energy opportunities and communication with Earth.
details:
Lunar Window is an interactive web-based tool that helps users compare potential lunar landing locations near the Moon’s South Pole. It uses NASA/JPL Horizons (DE441) data to track the positions of the Sun and Earth and analyze their visibility over time. Users can explore different dates, compare three test locations, view interactive graphs, and rank locations based on mission priorities.

The project makes complex astronomical data easier to understand and supports early lunar mission planning by highlighting potential sunlight and Earth visibility opportunities. Its creative approach combines astronomical data, interactive visualization, and location comparison in one tool.

We developed the project using Python to retrieve and validate NASA data, and HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to build the interactive website. We also used the NASA/JPL Horizons API and ChatGPT assistance during development. Our team considered data reliability, visibility conditions, usability, and the scientific limitations of the model.
